text:
anya: Heads-up — grafana panel for token-level latency (p50/p95/p99) shows a sharp p99 spike in eu-west-3 starting ~11:20 UTC. tokens/sec also dropped ~30% on affected shards. screenshot: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/abcd/token-slo?orgId=1&panelId=7 :eyes:
kevin: I can see the alert fired (ops-bot) at 11:22. Any errors in pod logs?
ops-bot: Alert: token_latency_p99{region="eu-west-3"} > 450ms for 5m — fired at 2026-03-18T11:22:11Z
sam: quick grab of exporter logs shows repeated TCP retransmits around that window. e.g. `tcp_retransmits_total` jumped on host gpu-node-12.
maria: also correlates with NIC driver churn from the infra deploy at 11:15 — rolling update hit a small subset of the pool.
anya: timeline: infra rolling update -> nic flaps on nodes servicing hot shards -> tokens/sec drop -> batching queues grow -> p99 climbs. Looks like queueing+networking not GPU starved.
kevin: can someone paste the promql? I want a per-shard breakdown.
sam: promql I used (short):
```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, shard, region, model))
```
then tokens/sec: `sum(rate(tokens_generated[5m])) by (shard, region)`
maria: suggestion: create a recording rule that pre-aggregates by (shard, region) to reduce query cost and make alerting more robust. Also lower the alert sensitivity to 1m->3m to reduce noise during rolling updates.
liz: we should also split the grafana panel to expose queue length and net_errors side-by-side. Right now p99 hides root cause.
anya: Agreed. Proposal: 1) add recording rule token_latency_p99_by_shard (1m scrape -> 5m recording) 2) new panel with columns: p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, queue_depth, net_retransmits. 3) short-term: silence token_latency_p99 alerts for eu-west-3 for 30m while infra rollback finishes.
kevin: For silencing, can we use alertmanager inhibition for rolling deploy tag? ops-bot, can you add a silence keyed to `deploy=rolling`?
ops-bot: Creating silence now for token_latency_p99 in eu-west-3 for 30m. ID: silence-3287.
sam: Also saw k8s kube-proxy churn on those nodes — connection tracking entries were high. Might be kernel conntrack exhaustion. Command `conntrack -S` shows 95% usage on gpu-node-12.
maria: If conntrack is the issue we need a two-pronged fix: tune conntrack on NICs (increase max) and add a DaemonSet to opportunistically clear stale entries when safe. But robust fix is to land the kernel NIC driver patch from infra team.
liz: For cost impact: when tokens/sec drops, per-token unit cost increases due to lower GPU utilization + more queueing. Estimate: ~12% cost bump for eu-west-3 during the incident window. We should include cost delta in the post-incident note.
anya: Action items: A) eng-platform: add recording rule + new composite panel (assigned: liz) B) eng-sre: investigate conntrack tuning and kernel patch (assigned: sam) C) infra: roll back or reapply NIC driver with patch (ping infra@) D) product: decide whether to route some traffic to eu-west-1 as temporary capacity (maria to loop in)
kevin: I'll update the runbook: add a checklist for rolling updates: 1) shard drain, 2) monitor conntrack, 3) stagger NIC restarts.
maria: Also recommend adjusting autoscale policy: prefer GPU-burst fallback to adjacent region before queueing grows > 200ms p95. Might save cost and avoid SLA hits.
anya: One more note — recording rules reduce Prometheus CPU but we must watch cardinality: group by only (shard, region, model_family) not full model id.
sam: temporary workaround: pin hot shards away from hosts with older NIC firmware via nodeSelector until infra patch lands.
liz: I'll sketch the new panel layout and open a PR for the recording rule. PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/observability/pulls/456
deploy-bot: Deploy started for observability infra PR#456 at 11:50 UTC — status: queued.
kevin: thanks everyone. if we don't see recovery in 15m we escalate to infra oncall. :thumbsup:
